tagline: Prove the bug before fixing it, fix it where it originates — then prove the fix with the same probe.
summary: A fix you cannot demonstrate is a guess. proof-of-fix enforces the evidence-first loop: record the smallest probe that demonstrates the bug (accepted only if it FAILS), name the commit that introduced it, fix the code at that origin, then check — the exact same probe must now run green, on a fix that edits a file the origin commit changed. It engages on its own: a bug-shaped prompt (en/fr) injects the protocol into context once per session per repo, and a Stop hook re-runs an open repro itself — auto-closing it on a green run at the origin with a one-line confirmation, asking for the origin when a green fix sits beside the defect, handing the failing output back to the session on red (one attempt per work-state, capped, never a Stop loop). The recommended probe is a real test committed with the fix, so every repro becomes a permanent regression guard. State lives in .git and is never committed; opt out per repo.
capabilities: record: runs the reproduction probe and REFUSES it if it exits 0 — a repro must fail before the fix, or it proves nothing
origin: declares the commit that introduced the defect (or first added the faulty code); a fix that cannot land in its files is declared with its reason
check: re-runs the exact same probe — the fix is proven only by a green run of the command that was red, on a fix that edits a file the origin commit changed
Auto-engagement: bug/fix-shaped prompts (en + fr) inject the protocol as context, once per session per repo

Stop guard with real signals: an open repro is re-run by the hook itself — green at the origin auto-proves it, green beside the origin blocks until the origin is named, red blocks with the failing output (bounded per work-state, capped at 5)
Horizontal: any repo, any stack — the probe is whatever command demonstrates the bug; git + Python stdlib only
